title: JavaScript this Core Check
description: Check your understanding of how this is determined, method calls, lost context, strict mode, and arrow-function this.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: In most regular function calls, what determines the value of `this`?

options.text: The file where the function is defined

questions.explanation: `this` is usually determined by the call site: how the function is called.
The function is called as `user.sayName()`, so `this` is `user`.
For a method call, `this` is usually the object before the dot.
The function is called as `admin.sayName()`, so `this` is `admin`, even though the function came from `user`.

questions.prompt: What commonly happens when an object method is stored in a variable and then called as a plain function?

options.text: It always keeps the original object as `this`
It may lose its original `this` context
It becomes an arrow function automatically

questions.explanation: Assigning a method to a variable copies the function value, not the original method call context.

questions.prompt: In strict mode, what is `this` inside a plain regular function call like `showThis()`?
questions.explanation: In strict mode, a plain regular function call has `this` set to `undefined`.

questions.prompt: What is special about arrow functions and `this`?

options.text: Arrow functions always set `this` to the object before the dot
Arrow functions do not have their own `this`; they use lexical `this`
Arrow functions can only be used inside classes

questions.explanation: Arrow functions capture `this` from the surrounding scope instead of creating their own.

questions.prompt: Which object method style is best when the method needs to use `this`?
questions.explanation: Method shorthand creates a regular method whose `this` is set by the method call.

questions.prompt: Why can an arrow function be useful inside a method's callback?

options.text: It can inherit the method's surrounding `this`
It makes `this` point to the callback itself
It prevents the callback from running

questions.explanation: Arrow callbacks are useful when they should use the `this` from the surrounding method.

questions.prompt: Which tool creates a new function with fixed `this` for later use?
questions.explanation: `bind()` returns a new function with a fixed `this` value.

questions.prompt: Which tool calls a function immediately with a chosen `this` and arguments passed one by one?
questions.explanation: `call()` invokes the function immediately and accepts arguments one by one after the `this` value.

questions.prompt: Which tool calls a function immediately with a chosen `this` and arguments passed as an array?
questions.explanation: `apply()` invokes the function immediately and receives the function arguments as an array or array-like value.
